sections.h: Pick the right bracket before the technician arrives

A bracket rated well above the weight of your TV is safer than one at its limit.

sections.h: Before you spray: scout, identify, decide
p: Walk the field early, look under the leaves, note which pest or disease you see and how widespread it is, and spray only when the problem needs it. A wrong diagnosis wastes money and can harm the crop, so identify the problem before you choose a product.

sections.h: Safe spraying habits
p: Read the label for the dose, the crop, the waiting period before harvest and the re-entry time. Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and long clothing. Mix in a ventilated place, never eat or smoke while spraying, and spray when it is calm rather than windy or about to rain. Rinse equipment away from water sources and store chemicals locked and out of reach of children.

sections.h: A simple repair or replace rule of thumb
p: If the repair costs more than about half the price of a comparable new appliance, or the appliance is old and has failed repeatedly, replacing it often makes more sense. A diagnosis, a written quote and the age of the appliance help you decide. Ask whether spare parts are available before you agree to a repair.

sections.h: Before you call a technician
p: Check the plug, the socket and the breaker. Read any error code on the display and note when the fault happens. For fridges, check the door seals and the vents. For washing machines, check the drain filter. A clear description saves time and can reduce the diagnosis cost.

sections.h: Signs of a failing water heater
p: No hot water, a breaker that trips when the heater switches on, water pooling around the tank, strange noises or rust-coloured water are all signs to call a technician. Switch the power off at the breaker first, and never open the unit while it is live.

sections.h: How to spot a hidden leak
p: Signs include a rising water bill, damp patches, mould, peeling paint and the sound of running water when every tap is off. To test, close all taps and check whether the water meter still moves. If it does, there is a leak somewhere.
